newsitem.title: USA: Three Midwest hog plants closed Monday.
newsitem.headline: Three Midwest hog plants closed Monday.

text.p: Three large U.S. Midwest hog slaughter plants will be closed on Monday, with two exercising floating holidays and the third switching to a four-day week because of tight hog supplies, company sources said.
Farmland Industries hog plant in Dubuque, Iowa, and ConAgra Inc subsidiary Swift and Co's plant in Marshalltown, Iowa will be observing a floating holiday.
"As part of their union contract, they get off the third Monday in July," said Farmland spokeswoman Sherlyn Manson about the Dubuque pork plant's planned closure.
A Swift and Co employee confirmed the Marshalltown, Iowa plant would be closed on Monday for a 'floater'.

American Foods Group Inc Dakota Pork Industries' hog plant in Huron, S.D., will be closed Monday as part of a cost-cutting move begun two weeks ago, said a plant official who asked not to be identified.
"Its mostly because of a lack of (hog) numbers out there," he said. "Until the numbers pick up, we will stay on the four day week Tuesday through Friday," the official said.
The four-day week could last until early September, he said.

Estimated daily slaughter capacity at the plants were about 14,000-16,000 head for Swift's Marshalltown, Iowa facility, near 10,000 for Farmland's Dubuque, Iowa plant and about 7,500 for the Dakota Pork plant in Huron, S.D., industry sources said.
